questions.q: State property P3: \(\int_a^b f(x)dx = \int_a^b f(a+b-x)dx\). Write the substitution used to prove it.
questions.a: The substitution is \(t = a+b-x\), so \(dt = -dx\). When \(x=a\), \(t=b\); when \(x=b\), \(t=a\). Then \(\int_a^b f(x)dx = \int_b^a f(a+b-t)(-dt) = \int_a^b f(a+b-t)dt = \int_a^b f(a+b-x)dx\). A wrong answer (e.g., \(t = x-a\) or forgetting the minus sign) reveals the student does not understand how the limits flip and the differential changes sign, which is the core of the proof.

questions.q: Explain why \(\int_{-2}^2 x^3 dx = 0\) without computing the antiderivative. Which property justifies this?
questions.a: The function \(f(x)=x^3\) is odd because \(f(-x) = -x^3 = -f(x)\). By property P7(ii), \(\int_{-a}^a f(x)dx = 0\) for an odd function. Here \(a=2\). A wrong answer (e.g., saying it's because the function is symmetric) shows confusion between even and odd symmetry; the student must identify the function as odd, not just symmetric.

questions.q: Evaluate \(\int_0^{\pi} \frac{x \sin x}{1+\cos^2 x} dx\) using property P4.
questions.a: Let \(I = \int_0^{\pi} \frac{x \sin x}{1+\cos^2 x} dx\). By P4, \(I = \int_0^{\pi} \frac{(\pi-x) \sin(\pi-x)}{1+\cos^2(\pi-x)} dx = \int_0^{\pi} \frac{(\pi-x) \sin x}{1+\cos^2 x} dx\) (since \(\sin(\pi-x)=\sin x\), \(\cos(\pi-x)=-\cos x\)). Adding the two expressions: \(2I = \int_0^{\pi} \frac{\pi \sin x}{1+\cos^2 x} dx\). Substitute \(t=\cos x\), \(dt = -\sin x dx\): when \(x=0\), \(t=1\); \(x=\pi\), \(t=-1\). Then \(2I = \pi \int_1^{-1} \frac{-dt}{1+t^2} = \pi \int_{-1}^1 \frac{dt}{1+t^2} = \pi [\tan^{-1} t]_{-1}^1 = \pi (\frac{\pi}{4} - (-\frac{\pi}{4})) = \frac{\pi^2}{2}\). So \(I = \frac{\pi^2}{4}\). A wrong answer (e.g., forgetting to change limits in the \(t\)-substitution or misapplying \(\sin(\pi-x)\)) reveals gaps in trigonometric identities combined with property application.

questions.q: Compare the use of P3 and P4. When would you choose P4 over P3? Give an example integral where P4 is directly applicable but P3 would require extra work.
questions.a: P4 is the special case of P3 when \(a=0\) and \(b=a\), i.e., the lower limit is 0. P4 states \(\int_0^a f(x)dx = \int_0^a f(a-x)dx\). Choose P4 when the integral has limits \([0,a]\) because the transformation \(x \to a-x\) is simpler to write and remember. Example: \(\int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin x}{\sin x + \cos x} dx\). Using P4 with \(a=\pi/2\) gives \(\int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{\cos x}{\cos x + \sin x} dx\); adding yields \(\int_0^{\pi/2} 1 dx = \pi/2\), so original integral is \(\pi/4\). Using P3 with \(a=0, b=\pi/2\) gives the same but P4 is more direct. A wrong answer (e.g., saying P3 and P4 are identical) shows the student hasn't recognized the special-case relationship and the efficiency of P4 for \([0,a]\) limits.

questions.q: A student writes: \(\int_{-1}^1 \frac{1}{x^2} dx = \left[ -\frac{1}{x} \right]_{-1}^1 = -1 - 1 = -2\). Evaluate this solution. Is the property P7 applicable? Why or why not?
questions.a: The solution is incorrect because \(f(x)=1/x^2\) is not continuous on \([-1,1]\) (it has an infinite discontinuity at \(x=0\)). The definite integral is improper and diverges. Property P7 requires \(f\) to be integrable on \([-a,a]\); here it is not. The student blindly applied the even-function property (P7(i)) without checking continuity/integrability. A wrong evaluation (e.g., saying the answer is \(-2\) or \(0\)) reveals the student ignores the domain condition for definite integrals and applies properties mechanically.

questions.q: Create a definite integral problem that requires using both P2 (additivity) and P7 (even/odd) to evaluate efficiently. Provide the integrand, limits, and the final answer.
questions.a: Example: Evaluate \(\int_{-2}^2 (|x| + x^3) dx\). Split using P2: \(\int_{-2}^2 |x| dx + \int_{-2}^2 x^3 dx\). \(|x|\) is even, so first integral \(= 2\int_0^2 x dx = 2 \cdot \frac{4}{2} = 4\). \(x^3\) is odd, so second integral \(= 0\). Total \(= 4\). A poor answer would be an integral that doesn't need both properties (e.g., just an even function on \([-a,a]\)), showing the student cannot design a problem that combines concepts.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The properties of definite integrals are a set of algebraic and symmetry rules that allow manipulation of definite integrals without explicitly finding ______.
Fill in the blank: To begin any problem: (1) Identify the limits and the ______.
Fill in the blank: To begin any problem: (______) Identify the limits and the integrand.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can also prove each property using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus or a direct substitution.
